why: I checked both briefs against the two must_not items. The verifier brief passes: its PASS/FAIL for Check 1 asks only for `RETURNED {}` and `exit=0`. The checks on the stderr line, file name and position appear only under "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)", so item 1 is not broken. The builder brief breaks item 2. Step 2 tells the builder to do more than return {} on a parse error: "when the parse fails, write one line to stderr before returning {}. The line must name the path and include the parse error message". The expect line only asks for the parse error to be caught and {} returned. A required warning that names the file and position is the extra behaviour the must_not list warns about (item 1 names "logging a warning" as going too far). Step 4's README text about "prints a warning naming the file" adds to the same overreach.
